subject: Re: Pilot credits & burn-rate check next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@acme-robotics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 15:00:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot credits & burn-rate check post-call recap

Hi Emily -

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the pilot:

Summary from our call
- Goal: Validate on-device assistant flows and summarize cost/latency tradeoffs before Q4 product launch.
- Pilot window: 4 weeks (we've currently got 2 weeks remaining on the trial).
- Expected steady-state tokens: ~5M tokens/month (inference + chat history).
- Peak/burst: up to 20M tokens in a heavy-test phase (2-3 days).
- Expected unit economics target: target <= $1,000 per 1M tokens for production scale; for pilot we discussed pricing guidance and credits to bridge evaluation.

Open asks (what we need from you)
1) Confirm anticipated average and peak token volumes (you mentioned "~5M/mo, up to 20M burst").
2) Budget range for a 3-6 month production pilot (rough $/month).
3) Any procurement timelines or paperwork we should factor in if we extend the pilot (PO, SOW, vendor form).

What we can do now
- I can escalate a one-time credits extension to cover the remaining pilot + a 2-week extension for heavy testing.
- I will include Rishi (Solutions) to help size the best model/quantization profile so we meet your cost target.

Attachments: I attached a sample SOW and a simple pricing model worksheet so you can plug in your estimated volumes (pilot-sow.pdf, pricing-model.xlsx).

Next steps
- Emily: confirm token volumes + budget range (reply inline).
- Marissa/Rishi: provide formal credits extension amount and conditions by EOD Thursday.

Thanks - talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0192

Subject: Re: Pilot credits & burn-rate check post-call recap

Hi Marissa -

Thanks for the recap, that aligns with our internal notes. Quick answers inline:

1) Token volumes
- Baseline: 4-6M tokens/month (we expect ~5M).
- Heavy test (integration/event loads): up to ~18-22M tokens over a 48-72 hour window.

2) Budget range
- For an extended pilot / pre-prod run the team has signaled a budget of $12k- $18k/month. Our finance team is conservative, so we need to see unit economics before committing higher.

3) Procurement
- We typically need a simple SOW + PO. Procurement may take 2-3 weeks if we move to a contract. For a credits extension, procurement prefers a short one-page approval memo.

Credits extension ask
- Can Redwood provide $10k in trial credits to cover the next 2 weeks of heavy testing (so we can validate burst behaviour)? If approved, we can schedule the heavy tests for the week of May 18.

Happy to loop procurement if you need the PO path.

Thanks,
Emily Chen
Product Lead - Assistant Platform
Acme Robotics
emily.chen@acme-robotics.com

Subject: Re: Pilot credits & burn-rate check credits extension approval

Hi Emily -

Good news: I approved a one-time $10,000 credit extension to cover the heavy-testing window and the following week. A few notes/conditions:
- Credits valid for 30 days from date of activation.
- Credits apply to hosted API usage only (not to Dedicated or professional services).
- We request a quick summary of test dates and token burn after the heavy test so we can capture learnings for model recommendations.

I attached a short approval memo for your procurement team (credits-extension-approval.pdf). If procurement prefers a PO path, we can accept a PO referencing deal RDW-2389 and apply credits on receipt.

Rishi - looping you in to confirm model config suggestions and to help set the test plan.

Action items
- Emily: confirm heavy-test dates (May 18-20 proposed).
- Marissa: I'll push the credit activation and send confirmation when it's live.
- Rishi: propose model/quant settings for the pilot (low-latency vs low-cost tradeoffs).

I'll follow up with DocuSign link if procurement needs a signed memo.

Best,
Marissa
